rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening إذ recalls the event by an implicit verb, as in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: في الآية المتقدمة: هي منصوبة بفعل مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats Iblis as a non-angel, making his exclusion disconnected.
rows.anchor: واختلف في قوله إلا إبليس فقيل هو استثناء منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view regards Iblis as an angel, making the exception connected.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو متصل لأن إبليس من الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭīnan may be a specification or circumstantial description.
rows.anchor: وقوله طينا يصح أن يكون تمييزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis wrongly judged fire superior to clay, overlooking that God assigns excellence independently of origins.
rows.anchor: وقاس إبليس في هذه النازلة فأخطأ، وذلك أنه رأى الفضيلة لنفسه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports Ibn Abbas’s view that Iblis was commanded to take Adam’s clay from earth.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن ابن عباس أن إبليس هو الذي أمره الله فأخذ من الأرض طينة آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common account identifies the one who took Adam’s clay as the Angel of Death.
rows.anchor: والمشهور أنه ملك الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s disbelief arose from failing to recognize God’s justice; pride and envy motivated his refusal.
rows.anchor: وكفر إبليس في أن جهل صفة العدل من الله تعالى، حين لحقته الأنفة، والكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says envy was the first means by which God was disobeyed, appearing in Iblis.
rows.anchor: وكان أصل ذلك الحسد، ولذلك قيل: إن أول ما عصي الله بالحسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis’s claim that he was better than Adam makes the wrongdoing explicit, as also stated elsewhere.
rows.anchor: من قوله أرأيتك هذا الذي كرمت علي أنا خير منه [الأعراف: 11]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf in arāʾaytaka is an emphatic address particle with no grammatical position and is extra.
rows.anchor: والكاف في قوله أرأيتك هي كاف خطاب ومبالغة في التنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here arāʾayta means have you considered, alerting the listener to attend to what follows.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أرأيت: أتأملت ونحوه، كأن المخاطب بها ينبه المخاطب

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh takes arāʾaytaka to mean tell me; Ibn ʿAṭiyya accepts this when a question follows, but not here.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه: هي بمعنى أخبرني، ومثل بقوله أرأيتك زيدا أبو من هو؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Sibawayh’s analysis here, while noting al-Zajjaj cited the wording in 20:56 without an example.
rows.anchor: وقول سيبويه: صحيح حيث يكون بعدها استفهام كمثاله، وأما في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads akhkhartani with yāʾ in connection and pause, which the author calls original.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «أخرتني» بياء في الوصل والوقف، وهذا هو الأصل

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s line illustrates deletion of a final yāʾ in rhyme, unlike this verse.
rows.anchor: فهل يمنعني ارتياد البلاد ... من حذر الموت أن يأتين

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Nafiʿ and Abu ʿAmr retain the yāʾ in connection but omit it when pausing.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو بالياء في الوصل وبحذفها في الوقف

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers omit the yāʾ in both connection and pause, by analogy with a final yāʾ after kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي «أخرتن» بحذف الياء في الوصل والوقوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deleted yāʾ resembles the form in 11:105.
rows.anchor: وهذا تشبيه بياء قاض ونحوه، لكونها ياء متطرفة قبلها كسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La-aḥtanikan means I will lead or drive them, from placing a bridle under an animal’s jaw to make it obey.
rows.anchor: وقوله لأحتنكن معناه: لأميلن ولأجرن، وهو مأخوذ من تحنيك الدابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A phrase about tongues grazing wealth means consuming it; a poem about hardship illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: وألسنة تحتنك المال، أي تجتره، ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari explains the threat as I will utterly destroy them.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري لأحتنكن معناه: لاستأصلن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas paraphrases the threat as I will take control.
rows.anchor: وعبر ابن عباس في ذلك ب «لأستولين»

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd paraphrases the threat as I will lead them astray; the author says this substitutes wording rather than explaining it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد لأضلن، وهذا بدل اللفظ لا تفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis judged Adam’s descendants vulnerable because their constitution comes with desires and volatile traits; he excepted those firm in obedience.
rows.anchor: وحكم إبليس بهذا الحكم على ذرية آدم، من حيث رأى الخلقة مجوفة مختلفة الأجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Go and the following commands are imperatives used as threats, as in 41:40.
rows.anchor: وقوله: اذهب وما بعده من الأوامر، هو صيغة افعل من التهديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Iblis means following the unbelieving path he summons people to; the warning concerns unbelievers and sinners subject to it.
rows.anchor: وتبعك معناه في طريق الكفر الذي تدعو إليه، فالآية في الكفار وفي من ينفذ عليه الوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jazāʾ is a verbal noun functioning circumstantially, and mawfūr means complete.
rows.anchor: وقوله جزاء مصدر في موضع الحال، و «الموفور» المكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istafziz means make people lightheaded and deceive them until they fall into what you want; it derives from lightness.
rows.anchor: واستفزز معناه استخف واخدع حتى يقع في إرادتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A line by Zuhayr illustrates the lexical usage of istifzāz.
rows.anchor: ومن الخفة قيل لولد البقرة فز ومثله قول زهير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets Satan’s voice as singing, instruments, and amusements associated with sin.
rows.anchor: قيل هو الغناء والمزامير والملاهي، لأنها أصوات كلها مختصة بالمعاصي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas takes Satan’s voice as every caller summoning people to disobey God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: صوته، كل داع إلى معصية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers an inclusive reading that covers all these sounds and calls.
rows.anchor: والصواب أن يكون الصوت يعم جميع ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajlib means raise a frightening clamor; al-Hasan reads it with joined hamza and ḍamma on the lām.
rows.anchor: وقوله وأجلب أي هول والجلبة: الصوت الكثير المختلط الهائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cavalry and foot soldiers may be metaphor for full effort, literal jinn forces per Qatada, or human agents of falsehood per Mujahid.
rows.anchor: وقوله بخيلك ورجلك قيل هذا مجاز واستعارة، بمعنى: اسع سعيك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Iblis literally has cavalry and infantry among the jinn.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه: أن له من الجن خيلا ورجلا، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies cavalry and footmen as human agents in falsehood who aid Iblis.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد: فرسان الناس ورجالتهم، المتصرفون في الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers use a still jīm for rajil as a collective; Hafs and others read kasra as an adjective for a walker; Qatada and ʿIkrima read the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «ورجلك» بسكون الجيم، وهو جمع راجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anonymous poem illustrates rajilan as describing walking without riding.
rows.anchor: أنا أقاتل عن ديني على فرسي ... ولا كذا رجلا إلا بأصحابي

rows.speaker: قتادة وعكرمة
rows.claim: Qatada and ʿIkrima read wa-rijālaka in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة وعكرمة: «ورجالك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharing in wealth includes sinful financial uses such as forbidden livestock, prostitution fees, wine, soothsayers, and usury.
rows.anchor: وشاركهم في الأموال عام: لكل معصية يصنعها الناس بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharing in offspring includes illicit conception, pagan names, burying daughters alive, and corrupting children through unbelieving religions.
rows.anchor: وقوله والأولاد عام لكل ما يصنع في أمر الذرية من المعاصي

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash’s report that intercourse with jinn can impregnate a human woman is weak.
rows.anchor: وما أدخل النقاش من وطء الجن وأنه تحبل المرأة من الإنس فضعيف كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s promises deceive with false assurances, including denial of resurrection, sharing in people’s inner lives.
rows.anchor: وقوله وعدهم أي منهم بما لا يتم لهم، وبأنهم غير مبعوثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: My servants means believers protected from unbelief and the God-fearing protected from sins; the special address honors them though it can include all creation.
rows.anchor: وقوله عبادي يريد المؤمنين في الكفر، والمتقين في المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The special address resembles a father calling a favored child my son to distinguish him.
rows.anchor: كما يقول رجل لأحد بنيه إذا رأى منه ما يحب: هذا ابني

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet called Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas his maternal uncle and challenged others to show an uncle like him.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لسعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulṭān means sovereignty and control; explaining it as proof here is strained.
rows.anchor: و «السلطان» الملكة والتغلب، وتفسيره هنا بالحجة قلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sufficient as guardian of believers and sustainer of their guidance.
rows.anchor: وكفى بربك يا محمد حافظا للمؤمنين، وقيما على هدايتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yuzjī means slowly moving something heavy or weak; camels and clouds are described this way, with al-Farazdaq’s poem as evidence.
rows.anchor: سوق الثقيل السير، إما لضعف أو ثقل حمل أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bāḍāʿa muzjāt is defective merchandise needing recommendation or help to be accepted.
rows.anchor: والبضاعة المزجاة هي التي تحتاج لاختلالها أن تساق بشفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God drives ships with gentle winds and oars; falak and baḥr broadly mean ships and abundant water, fresh or salt.
rows.anchor: وإزجاء الفلك سوقه بالريح اللينة والمجاديف، والفلك والبحر الماء الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God’s bounty includes livelihood and reward through pilgrimage, jihad, and similar pursuits.
rows.anchor: وقوله لتبتغوا من فضله لفظ يعم البصر، وطلب الأجر، في حج أو غزو ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sea travel is permissible for pilgrimage, jihad, and livelihood; scholars differ on required long sea travel for pilgrimage and on sailing merely to increase wealth.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف في جواز ركوبه للحج والجهاد والمعاش، واختلف في وجوبه للحج

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet said he would never sail; Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows personal judgment or revelation as its basis.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عنه أنه قال «البحر لا أركبه أبدا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse calls attention to God’s favors and generosity toward His servants.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية توقيف على آلاء الله وفضله عند عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍurr covers fear of drowning and inability to travel; its worst form is violent sea agitation.
rows.anchor: والضر لفظ يعم خوف الغرق، والامتساك في المشي، وأهول حالاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalla means lost or destroyed, belittling idols: people innately know they cannot act in grave crises, as the sea demonstrates.
rows.anchor: وقوله ضل معناه تلف وفقد، وهي عبارة تحقير لمن يدعي إلها من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When safe, people turn away without reflecting on God’s action when they needed Him; kafūr means ungrateful.
rows.anchor: أعرضتم أي لم تفكروا في صنع الله وقت حاجتكم إليه، وقوله كفورا أي بالنعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān is humanity generally, since no one fully gives God the thanks due; al-Zajjaj’s restriction to unbelievers is weak.
rows.anchor: والإنسان هنا للجنس، وكل أحد لا يكاد يؤدي شكر الله تعالى كما يجب

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets the human as unbelievers, a reading Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls unconvincing.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج الإنسان يراد به الكفار، وهذا غير بارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question warns those forgetting sea distress that God can make the ground swallow them when they are at ease on land.
rows.anchor: المعنى أفأمنتم أيها المعرضون الناسون الشدة، حين صرتم إلى الرخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥāṣib is a storm throwing hail, stones, or similar missiles; poems and the fate of Lot’s people illustrate it.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحاصب الذي أصاب قوم لوط، والحصب

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use third-person yāʾ for the sequence of verbs about sinking, sending, returning, and drowning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «يخسف» بالياء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read that verb sequence with first-person plural nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ذلك كله بالنون

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ومجاهد
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Mujahid read tughriqukum with feminine t, referring to the wind.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ومجاهد «تغرقكم» بالتاء أي الريح

rows.speaker: حميد
rows.claim: Humayd reads nughriqukum with nūn and assimilates qāf into kāf; also reported from Abu ʿAmr and Ibn Muhaysin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حميد «نغرقكم» بالنون حقيقة وأدغم القاف في الكاف

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Rajaʾ read yughriqukum with doubled rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء «يغرقكم» بشد الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakīl means caretaker, qāṣif one who breaks what it meets, tāra another time; Abu Jaʿfar reads winds in plural.
rows.anchor: و «الوكيل» القائم بالأمور، و «القاصف» الذي يكسر كل ما يلقى ويقصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabīʿ is someone pursuing vengeance or a debt; a poem and Prophetic report illustrate following up a claim, so none will seek retaliation against God’s act.
rows.anchor: و «التبيع» الذي يطلب ثأرا أو دينا، ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We honored means God endowed humanity with dignity and excellence, not wealth, as a fine garment is called noble for its qualities.
rows.anchor: كرمنا تضعيف كرم، فالمعنى: جعلنا لهم كرما، أي شرفا وفضلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse lists human distinctions; animals and jinn are the many less-favored creatures, while angels are outside that group.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية، عدد الله تعالى فيها على بني آدم ما خصهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans carry themselves on land and sea by intention, purpose, and planning, unlike other animals.
rows.anchor: وحملهم في البر والبحر، مما لا يصلح لحيوان سوى بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human provision is broader because people earn money, wear clothes, and prepare foods; provision is anything beneficial.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يكسبون المال خاصة دون الحيوان، ويلبسون الثياب

rows.speaker: جماعة
rows.claim: A group cites eating with hands, and another elevated sight and upright walking, as human distinctions; the author calls this inadequate because animals excel in other traits.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن جماعة أنهم قالوا: «التفضيل» هو أن يأكل بيديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True honor lies in intellect, by which humans know God, understand revelation, and reach bliss.
rows.anchor: وإنما التكريم والتفضيل بالعقل الذي يملك به الحيوان كله، وبه يعرف الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group infers angels outrank humans because they are excluded from the many over whom humans are favored.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: هذه الآية تقضي بفضل الملائكة على الإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bi-imāmihim can mean called by their imam’s name or brought accompanied by their imam.
rows.anchor: وقوله بإمامهم يحتمل أن يريد باسم إمامهم، ويحتمل أن يريد مع إمامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading calls people as communities; the second brings each community with a guide or misleader.
rows.anchor: فعلى التأويل الأول: يقال يا أمة محمد، ويا أتباع فرعون

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada identify the imam as the community’s prophet.
rows.anchor: فقال مجاهد وقتادة: نبيهم

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the imam as the revealed scripture given to the community.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد كتابهم الذي نزل عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan identify the imam as the book recording people’s deeds.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن: كتابهم الذي فيه أعمالهم

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group understands imam as the person followed, whether guide or misleader.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: متبعهم، من هاد أو مضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imam can cover these meanings because it is whatever one follows for guidance, like a builder’s line or road.
rows.anchor: ولفظة «الإمام» تعم هذا كله، لأن الإمام هو ما يؤتم به ويهتدى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet’s drinking-arrow comparison illustrates imam as a guiding builder’s line.
rows.anchor: ومنه قيل لخيط البناء إمام، قال الشاعر يصف قدحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not require angelic superiority; angels may be superior or equal, and their superiority is established elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وهذا غير لازم من الآية بل التفضيل بين الإنس والجن لم تعن به الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm may be an adverb with an implicit verb, attached to not being wronged, attached to God’s favoring, or treated as a built nominative subject.
rows.anchor: يحتمل قوله يوم أن يكون منصوبا على الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most say nadʿū with majestic nūn; Mujahid reads yadʿū, and al-Hasan has dialectal forms including nominative kull.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «ندعو» بنون العظمة، وقرأ مجاهد «يدعو»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unās is a collective noun without a singular from the same form.
rows.anchor: وأناس اسم جمع لا واحد له من لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The records are literal: believers receive them in the right, unbelievers in the left; warned sinners learn they will not remain in Hell forever.
rows.anchor: حقيقة في أن في يوم القيامة صحائف تتطاير وتوضع في الأيمان لأهل الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the book expresses joy in it, turning it over and considering it.
rows.anchor: وقوله يقرؤن كتابهم عبارة عن السرور بها أي يرددنها ويتأملونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not wronged a thread means no amount is withheld; the unspoken case follows the spoken case, as in 17:23 and 4:40.
rows.anchor: وقوله ولا يظلمون فتيلا أي ولا أقل ولا أكثر، فهذا هو مفهوم الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No reward for good deeds is reduced; fatīl is the thread in a date stone, proverbial for insignificance.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أنهم لا يبخسون من جزاء أعمالهم الصالحة شيئا

rows.speaker: محمد بن أبي موسى
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Musa takes this as the blessings of verse 70: blind to gratitude and belief here means blind about the afterlife.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن أبي موسى: الإشارة بهذه إلى النعم التي ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second blind may mean blindness like the first or a comparative degree; both refer to blindness of the heart.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أعمى الثاني أن يكون بمنزلة الأول، على أنه تشبيه بأعمى البصر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: They take this as worldly life and explain blindness as failure to see God’s signs and believe in His prophets.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد قتادة وابن زيد: الإشارة بهذه إلى الدنيا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the blind person in the afterlife has no proof to offer.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد «فهو في الآخرة أعمى» عن حجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers this to mean worldly life: one blind to God’s signs becomes more confused on Judgment Day, preserving the parallel with the right-hand book verse.
rows.anchor: والظاهر عندي أن الإشارة ب هذه إلى الدنيا، أي من كان في دنياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking in the afterlife to mean about the afterlife breaks the parallel between these verses.
rows.anchor: وإذا جعلنا قوله في الآخرة بمعنى في شأن الآخرة، لم تطرد المعادلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ on imāla of aʿmā; Abu ʿAmr inclines the first but opens the second, treating it as more blind.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بإمالة الأول وفتح الثاني، وتأوله بمعنى أشد عمى

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says imāla suits word-final forms, while aʿmā is incomplete as a comparative unless a comparison follows.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: لأن الإمالة إنما تحسن في الأواخر، وأعمى ليس كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʾḍallu supports a comparative reading: unbelievers can still believe in this life but not the next, where they are more lost and nearer punishment.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعله في الآخرة أضل سبيلا، لأن الكافر في الدنيا يمكن أن يؤمن فينجو

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh’s denial of more blind applies to physical blindness, not blindness of the heart where degrees vary.
rows.anchor: وقول سيبويه رحمه الله: لا يقال أعمى من كذا كما يقال ما أبداه

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makkī says the first blindness is physical blindness from guidance; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this clearly mistaken.
rows.anchor: وذكر مكي في هذه الآية، أن العمى الأول هو عمى العين عن الهدى

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh reads in as the lightened emphatic particle and the lām as emphasis; al-Farraʾ instead takes in as negation and lām as except.
rows.anchor: إن هذه عند سيبويه هي المخففة من الثقيلة، واللام في قوله ليفتنونك لام تأكيد

rows.speaker: ابن جبير ومجاهد
rows.claim: They say Quraysh asked the Prophet to touch their idols too before the Black Stone, offering a reciprocal gesture.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن جبير ومجاهد: نزلت الآية لأنهم قالوا لرسول الله

rows.speaker: الطبري وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and others say the Prophet considered outward agreement while inwardly rejecting the request, and revelation then came.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري وغيره: فهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يظهر لهم ذلك، وقلبه منكر

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others say Quraysh’s leaders offered compromise, echoing the warning in 68:9.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق وغيره، إنهم اجتمعوا إليه ليلة فعظموه، وقالوا له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say Thaqif asked to keep worshiping al-Lat for a year after conversion and retain gifts, suggesting the Prophet attribute permission to revelation.
rows.anchor: لأنهم طلبوا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يؤخرهم بعد إسلامهم سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Thaqif account would make the verse Medinan, while other accounts make it Meccan.
rows.anchor: ويلزم قائل هذا القول أن يجعل الآية مدنية، وقد روي ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All requests in the reports were contradicted by revelation; complying would fabricate religion because the Prophet’s actions and words are law.
rows.anchor: وجميع ما أريد من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بحسب هذا الاختلاف قد أوحى الله إليه خلافه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that they would take him as close friend recalls God’s rescue from compromise and alliance with unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقوله وإذا لاتخذوك خليلا توقيف على ما نجاه الله منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s making the Prophet steadfast is counted as a favor.
rows.anchor: وقوله لولا أن ثبتناك الآية، تعديد نعمة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have prayed not to be left to himself even for an instant.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت هذه الآية قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukūn means leaning supportively on a matter or settling toward it, as one leans on a wall’s corner; compare 11:80.
rows.anchor: و «الركون» شد الظهر إلى الأمر أو الحزم على جهة السكون إليه

rows.speaker: ابن مصرف وقتادة وعبد الله بن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: They read tarkan with ḍamma on kāf; most readers use fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «تركن» بفتح الكاف، وقرأ ابن مصرف وقتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet did not actually incline; he only had a fleeting impulse to win them over, and almost plus a little show it did not take root.
rows.anchor: ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يركن، لكنه كاد بحسب همه بموافقتهم

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says they nearly reported that the Prophet had inclined; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects this strained reading because a little contradicts it.
rows.anchor: وذهب ابن الأنباري إلى أن معناه لقد كاد أن يخبروا عنك أنك ركنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fleeting thought is likened to Joseph’s thought, and the two passages should be understood alike.
rows.anchor: وهذا الهم من النبي عليه السلام إنما كانت خطرة مما لا يمكن دفعه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: They explain the doubled life and death as doubled punishment in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: يريد ضعف عذاب الحياة وضعف عذاب الممات

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj also reports a request that the Prophet expel his poor companions.
rows.anchor: وحكى الزجاج أن الآية قيل إنها فيما أرادوه من طرد فقراء أصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment due to a sinner in both worlds would be doubled for the Prophet; doubling also applies to reward, suffering, and punishment of his wives.
rows.anchor: على معنى أن ما يستحقه هذا المذنب من عقوبتنا في الدنيا والآخرة كنا نضعفه لك

rows.speaker: حضرمى
rows.claim: Hadrami says the pronoun refers to Medina’s Jews, including Huyay ibn Akhtab, who urged the Prophet to move to Syria, where God would protect him from Romans.
rows.anchor: قال حضرمي الضمير في كادوا ليهود المدينة وناحيتها، كحيي بن أخطب وغيره

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says the Prophet set out for Dhu al-Hulayfa due to their suggestion; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects it as weak, unsupported by reliable biography and geographically implausible.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج بسبب قولهم، وعسكر بذي الحليفة

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: Another group takes the pronoun as Quraysh; al-Zajjaj relates it to their Dar al-Nadwa plot to kill the Prophet, making earth the whole world.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة الضمير في كادوا هو لقريش، وحكى الزجاج أن «استفزازهم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other accounts mean specifically Mecca or Medina, the place where people exercise their affairs, as in 5:33.
rows.anchor: وعلى سائر الأقوال هي أرض مخصوصة، إما مكة وإما المدينة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say Quraysh sought to expel the Prophet from Mecca after the boycott; they later harried him to emigrate, and the warning was fulfilled at Badr.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة: واستفزاز قريش هو ما كانوا ذهبوا إليه من إخراج رسول الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Quraysh intended expulsion but did not act because God wished to spare them; had they expelled him, they would have been punished.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد ذهبت قريش إلى هذا ولكنه لم يقع منها، لأنه لما أراد الله استبقاء قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat applies generally to all who sought to expel the Prophet.
rows.anchor: في يلبثون عام في جميعهم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: The Ibn Masʿud codex omits nūn so idhā governs the verb; other readers leave idhā inactive and retain nūn.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود «وإذا لا يلبثوا» بحذف النون، وإعمال إذا

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: ʿAta reads the verb with ḍamma on yāʾ and doubled bāʾ; Yaʿqub reports a similar reading with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عطاء بن أبي رباح «يلبثون» بضم الياء وفتح اللام وشد الباء

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAta reads after you where most readers have behind you; Ibn ʿAmir and others use khilāfaka with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عطاء «بعدك إلا قليلا» ، وقرأ الجمهور «خلفك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilāf means after; the author cites 9:81 and poetry, understanding an omitted genitive in each use.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى: فرح المخلفون بمقعدهم خلاف رسول الله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ parses sunnata with an omitted preposition, meaning like the custom; this requires continuing past a little.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء نصبه على حذف الخافض، لأن المعنى كسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s custom with past nations was punishment and destruction soon after they expelled their prophet.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية الإخبار أن سنة الله تعالى في الأمم الخالية وعادته أنها إذا أخرجت نبيها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes agree the command to establish prayer refers to obligatory prayers.
rows.anchor: هذه بإجماع من المفسرين إشارة إلى الصلوات المفروضة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وأبو بردة والحسن والجمهور
rows.claim: They read sun decline as noon, covering noon and afternoon; darkness covers evening and night; dawn recitation is morning prayer, so all prayers are covered.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عمر وابن عباس وأبو بردة والحسن والجمهور: «دلوك الشمس» زوالها

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports Gabriel came at sun decline and led the Prophet in noon prayer.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن مسعود أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «أتاني جبريل لدلوك الشمس

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet told Abu Bakr to go after the sun had declined, identifying that time as dulk.
rows.anchor: وروى جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من عنده وقد طعم وزالت الشمس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: They take sun decline as sunset, night darkness as ʿIsha, and dawn recitation as morning prayer, leaving noon and afternoon unmentioned.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود وابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading is preferable because it covers all prayers; both are linguistically valid since dulk is the sun’s slant from noon to sunset.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أصوب لعمومه الصلوات، وهما من جهة اللغة حسنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Arab used yudālik for leaning toward delay in repayment; poems illustrate the sun’s slant.
rows.anchor: ومن الدلوك الذي هو الميل قول الأعرابي للحسن بن أبي الحسن أيدالك الرجل امرأته

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والأصمعي وأبو عمرو الشيباني
rows.claim: They explain bi-rāḥ in poetry as the sun’s rays, shaded with the observer’s palm to see its angle.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة الأصمعي وأبو عمرو الشيباني ومعناه براحة الناظر يستكف بها أبدا

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reportedly explains dakat bi-rāḥ as a place called Barāḥ; Ibn ʿAṭiyya accepts this if truly transmitted from him.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن ابن مسعود أنه قال: دلكت براح يعني براح مكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghasaq means darkness gathering and thickening; Ibn Abbas says it begins at nightfall.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: غسق الليل بدؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾān of dawn may take an implicit recite, coordinate with prayer, or be exhortative; morning prayer is named for its long, audible recitation.
rows.anchor: ونصب قوله وقرآن بفعل مضمر تقديره واقرأ قرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn is witnessed by angels of night and day, as in the report that they meet at dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: وقوله إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا معناه ليشهده حفظة النهار وحفظة الليل من الملائكة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A famous report says night and day angels alternate and meet at dawn and afternoon prayers.
rows.anchor: يتعاقبون فيكم ملائكة بالليل وملائكة بالنهار، ويجتمعون في صلاة الصبح وصلاة العصر

rows.speaker: محمد بن سهل بن عسكر
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports via Abu al-Darda that Ibn ʿAskar says God and angels witness; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the report weak.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن سهل بن عسكر يشهده الله وملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min is partitive, meaning a time of night; the pronoun may refer to that implied time or the earlier Qurʾān of dawn.
rows.anchor: وقوله ومن الليل من للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tahajjad means cast sleep off oneself; hujūd is sleep, illustrated by poems.
rows.anchor: وفتهجد معناه: فاطرح الهجود عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb resembles words meaning to cast off a state; in 56:65 tafakkahūn means regret.
rows.anchor: وهذا الفعل جار مجرى تحوب وتأثم وتحنث، ومثله فظلتم تفكهون

rows.speaker: الأسود وعلقمة وعبد الرحمن بن الأسود
rows.claim: They say tahajjud follows a sleep.
rows.anchor: وقال الأسود وعلقمة وعبد الرحمن بن الأسود: «التهجد» بعد نومة

rows.speaker: الحجاج بن عمرو
rows.claim: Al-Hajjaj ibn ʿAmr says tahajjud is after a rest or sleep.
rows.anchor: وقال الحجاج بن عمرو إنما «التهجد» بعد رقدة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says tahajjud is what is performed after the final evening prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: «التهجد» ما كان بعد العشاء الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say nāfila laka is extra beyond the obligation, which they say applied to the Prophet’s night prayer.
rows.anchor: وقوله نافلة لك قال ابن عباس وغيره: معناه زيادة لك في الفرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, night prayer may be recommended, with the Prophet addressed and the community intended too.
rows.anchor: وتحتمل الآية أن يكون هذا على وجه الندب في التنفل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says night prayer is uniquely extra for the forgiven Prophet, while others use it to have sins removed; al-Tabari weakens this view.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: إنما هي نافلة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأنه مغفور له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forgiveness the Prophet’s additional prayers are virtues greater than the community’s extra worship, which compensates obligations or removes sins.
rows.anchor: فإنما كانت نوافله واستغفاره فضائل من العمل وقربا أشرف من نوافل أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even one without sins can perform extra worship as merit, such as a new Muslim or a child reaching puberty.
rows.anchor: وقد يتصور من لا ذنب له ينتفل فيكون تنفله فضيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praised station is the Prophet’s intercession; the prophets defer to him, and the extended report is in al-Bukhari and Muslim.
rows.anchor: وهو أمر الشفاعة الذي يتدافعه الأنبياء حتى ينتهي إليه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet said he is leader of Adam’s descendants, without boasting.
rows.anchor: أنا سيد، ولد آدم ولا فخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intercession report compresses stages: first intercession for reckoning and leaving the gathering, later for sinners after judgment and entry into Paradise or Hell.
rows.anchor: فمعناه الاقتضاب والاختصار. لأن الشفاعة في المذنبين لم تكن إلا بعد الحساب

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports the Prophet called the praised station the place where he intercedes for his community.
rows.anchor: وذكر الطبري عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash attributes three intercessions to the Prophet—general, precedence into Paradise, and for major sinners—while the famous view counts two.
rows.anchor: قال النقاش: لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث شفاعات

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A group including Mujahid says the praised station is God seating Muhammad with Him on the Throne.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن فرقة منها مجاهد أنها قالت: «المقام المحمود» هو أن الله عز وجل يجلس محمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says al-Tabari supports this with an excessive argument; it is remote except under subtle interpretation, though he does not reject its transmission outright.
rows.anchor: وعضد الطبري جواز ذلك بشطط من القول، وهو لا يخرج إلا على تلطف في المعنى

rows.speaker: أبو داود السختياني
rows.claim: Al-Sijistani says denial makes one suspect because scholars long transmitted it; Ibn ʿAṭiyya clarifies the issue is rejecting its possible interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر النقاش عن أبي داود السختياني أنه قال من أنكر هذا الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best reading is a broad prayer for God to improve every state and undertaking, including journeys, work, life, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: ظاهر هذه الآية والأحسن فيها أن يكون دعاء في أن يحسن الله حالته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: They read it as entering Medina and leaving Mecca; departure happened first, though arrival was the main goal.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة: أراد أدخلني المدينة وأخرجني من مكة

rows.speaker: أبو صالح ومجاهد
rows.claim: They interpret it as entering the work of conveying the law and leaving after full discharge.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو صالح ومجاهد: أدخلني في أمر تبليغ الشرع وأخرجني منه بالأداء التام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas also reads entry as death in the grave and exit as resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الإدخال بالموت في القبر والإخراج البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the general reading because it covers all specific interpretations.
rows.anchor: وما قدمت من العموم التام الذي يتناول هذا كله، أصوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most use ḍamma on mīm in madkhal and makhraj; others use fatḥa, requiring an implied intransitive entrance.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «مدخل» «ومخرج» بضم الميم، فهو جرى على أدخلني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣidq describes freedom from blame and completeness in praise.
rows.anchor: و «الصدق» هنا صفة تقتضي رفع المذام واستيعاب المدح

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Mujahid and others explain supporting authority as proof against unbelievers; al-Hasan and Qatada say power, leadership, and sword for religion.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد وغيره: حجة، يريد تنصرني ببيانها على الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet requested support by God’s command to aid religion; God promised and fulfilled it during and after his life.
rows.anchor: فطلب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك بأمر الله إياه به رغبة في نصر الدين

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies truth as the Qurʾān and falsehood as Satan; others identify faith and unbelief, or jihad and polytheism.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: الحق القرآن، والباطل الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author generalizes: revealed law is truth, unbelief is falsehood, and falsehood includes whatever cannot achieve a beneficial end.
rows.anchor: والصواب تعميم اللفظ بالغاية الممكنة، فيكون التفسير جاء الشرع بجميع ما انطوى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāna zahūqa is not limited to past time; falsehood has been and will continue to be vanquished.
rows.anchor: وقوله كان زهوقا ليست كان إشارة إلى زمن مضى، بل المعنى كان وهو يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though revealed in Mecca, the Prophet cited it while striking idols at the conquest, according to Ibn Hisham and others.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية نزلت بمكة، ثم إن رسول الله كان يستشهد بها يوم فتح مكة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Most use nūn in nunazzilu; Mujahid reads light yāʾ yunazzilu, also reported from Hafs by al-Marwazi.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «وننزل» بالنون، وقرأ مجاهد «وينزل» بالياء خفيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in min al-Qurʾān may mark origin or explain the kind of revelation; some reject partitive min lest some Qurʾān lack healing.
rows.anchor: وقوله من القرآن يصح أن تكون من لابتداء الغاية، ويصح أن تكون لبيان الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Partitive min is valid because revelation came in portions, each sharing the healing of the Qurʾān as a whole.
rows.anchor: بل يصح أن يكون للتبعيض بحسب أن إنزاله إنما هو مبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Healing is metaphorical: the Qurʾān removes doubts and lifts the heart’s cover to understand miracles, divine evidence, and law.
rows.anchor: واستعارته الشفاء للقرآن هو بحسب إزالته للريب وكشفه غطاء القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Healing may also mean benefit against illness through incantations and protective recitation.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد ب «الشفاء» نفعه من الأمراض بالرقى والتعويذ ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān is mercy but increases wrongdoers’ loss because they turn away unable to understand or receive instruction.
rows.anchor: وقوله ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا معنى أنه عليهم عمى، إذ هم معرضون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human may mean unbelievers in particular, using universal phrasing rhetorically; the preceding reference to wrongdoers supports the connection.
rows.anchor: الإنسان في هذه الآية لا يراد به العموم، وإنما يراد به بعضه وهم الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, humanity generally has this blameworthy trait, strongest in unbelievers and present in sinners too.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الإنسان في هذه الآية عاما للجنس، على معنى أن هذا الخلق الذميم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said of a believer: he turned away, so God turned away from him.
rows.anchor: وقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مؤمن: «فأعرض فأعرض الله عنه»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿraḍa means turning one’s side away and naʾā means moving far off, depicting abandonment of faith and gratitude.
rows.anchor: ومعنى أعرض ولانا عرضه، ونأى أي بعد، وهذه استعارة

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir alone reads wa-nāʾa; some take it as rising while turned aside, others as a reordered form of naʾā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحده «وناء» ، ومعناه نهض أي متباعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes nāʾa as arrogant self-separation from naʾā, distance and departure.
rows.anchor: والذي عندي أن «ناء ونأى» فعلان متباينان، وناء بجانبه عبارة عن التحيز والاستبداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When illness, financial loss, or other harm touches them, unbelievers despair because they do not believe in God or trust His control of events.
rows.anchor: ثم وصف الكفرة بأنهم إذا مسهم شر من مرض أو مصيبة في مال أو غير ذلك يئسوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person works according to a matching path, intention, school, and disposition; God knows best who is rightly guided.
rows.anchor: ثم قال عز وجل قل يا محمد كل يعمل على شاكلته أي على طريقته

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains shākilatihi as natural disposition and also intensity or manner.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: على شاكلته معناه على طبيعته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says direction, Qatada adds intention, and Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers these formulations.
rows.anchor: وأرجح هذه العبارات قول ابن عباس وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says shākilatihi means one’s religion.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: معناه على دينه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud’s Medina account says Jews asked about the spirit because their Torah reserved its knowledge to God; some warned against asking lest the answer displease them.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد الله بن مسعود، أنه كان مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فمر على حرث بالمدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet paused leaning on a palm stalk, then recited the verse; Ibn Masʿud thought revelation had come.
rows.anchor: قال فسألوه فوقف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم متوكئا على عسيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account makes the verse Meccan: Quraysh sent al-Nadr and ʿUqba to consult Jews, who suggested three test questions including the spirit.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية مكية والضمير لقريش، وذلك أنهم قالوا: نسأل عن محمد أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that account the Prophet promised a reply next day without saying if God wills; revelation paused fifteen days as correction.
rows.anchor: فيروى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لهم «غدا أخبركم به»

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority identify the spirit as the life-giving spirit in living beings, a difficult matter with no explanation; the author calls this correct.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة هي الجمهور: وقع السؤال عن الروح التي في الأشخاص الحيوانية ما هي؟

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the spirit as Gabriel and says Ibn Abbas concealed the view.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: الروح المسئول عنه جبريل، قال وكان ابن عباس يكتمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views identify the spirit as Jesus, an angel described in an elaborate report attributed to Ali, or the Qurʾān; the author doubts the report from Ali.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة عيسى ابن مريم، وقال علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min amr rabbī may mean the spirit is a divine matter reserved to God or that it came to be by His command.
rows.anchor: وقوله من أمر ربي يحتمل تأويلين: أحدهما

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: A report attributed to ʿAli describes an angel with immense numbers of faces, tongues, and languages; Ibn ʿAṭiyya doubts that it truly comes from ʿAli.
rows.anchor: ذكره الطبري، وما أظن هذا القول يصح عن علي

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group identifies the spirit as the Qurʾān; the author says the human-spirit explanation is clearest and most correct.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة الروح القرآن، وهذه كلها أقوال مفسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the first, human-spirit interpretation among the explanations.
rows.anchor: وهذه كلها أقوال مفسرة، والأول أظهرها وأصوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Except as mercy is a disconnected exception meaning but a mercy from your Lord preserves it; unlike a connected exception, it specifies something outside the same category.
rows.anchor: وقوله إلا رحمة استثناء منقطع، أي لكن رحمة من ربك تمسك ذلك عليك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والأعمش
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud and al-Aʿmash read wa-mā ūtū in third person; Ibn Masʿud also reports it from the Prophet, unlike the majority reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والأعمش «وما أوتوا» ، ورواها ابن مسعود عن النبي

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari’s heading takes the address as questioners and cites Qatada that they were Jews.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة: السائلون فقط، ترجم الطبري بذلك ثم أدخل تحت الترجمة عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others take the address as Jews collectively, matching Ibn Masʿud’s reading.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: المراد اليهود بجملتهم، وعلى هذا هي قراءة ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers that all people are addressed: the command to say the spirit is from God’s command addresses the whole world.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: العالم كله، وهذا هو الصحيح لأن قول الله له قل الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may include the Prophet and all people, whose knowledge is little compared with God’s.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أيضا أن تكون مخاطبة من الله للنبي ولجميع الناس

rows.speaker: الخضر
rows.claim: Al-Khidr compares created knowledge relative to God’s to a bird’s sip from the sea; Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers an alternate reading but calls it questionable.
rows.anchor: كما قال الخضر عليه السلام لموسى عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: When Jews asked whether you meant them or the Prophet’s people, he replied no, indicating all people; al-Tabari relates it.
rows.anchor: وقد نص رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله في بعض الأحاديث «كلا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this answered Jews who claimed the Torah gave great wisdom by comparing human learning to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقد قالت اليهود لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، كيف لم نؤت من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is linked to 31:27, where trees as pens would not exhaust God’s words.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى نزلت ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning rebukes the Prophet for promising an answer the next day; he must submit to God’s choice of what to reveal or withhold.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ولئن شئنا الآية فيها شدة على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهي عتاب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports a red wind from Syria removing Qurʾān from codices and hearts, citing this verse to show it is possible.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن مسعود أنه ستخرج ريح حمراء من قبل الشام فتزيل القرآن من المصاحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakīl is one who manages an affair, including advocacy, dispute, or arranging benefit.
rows.anchor: و «الوكيل» القائم بالأمر في الانتصار أو المخاصمة ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God counts His great favor in granting the Prophet prophethood and protecting him from polytheists.
rows.anchor: ثم عدد عليه عز وجل كبر فضله في اختصاصه بالنبوة وحمايته من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh asked for a miracle other than Qurʾān, claiming they could produce its like; the verse announces that humans and jinn cannot meet the challenge.
rows.anchor: سبب هذه الآية أن جماعة من قريش قالت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا محمد جئتنا بآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inimitability lies in composition and arrangement of meanings; exhaustive knowledge is God’s, while human limits prevent a matching arrangement.
rows.anchor: والعجز في معارضة القرآن إنما وقع في النظم والرصف لمعانيه، وعلة ذلك الإحاطة التي لا يتصف بها إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The negative response is syntactically independent, not an oath’s answer; conditional lām may be omitted or emphatic and the negative verb jussive.
rows.anchor: وقوله لا يأتون بمثله في موضع رفع، ولا متلقية قسما

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash’s line illustrates a jussive negative verb governed by the condition.
rows.anchor: لئن منيت بنا عن غر معركة ... لا تلفنا عن دماء القوم ننتقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓahīr means helper, linked to reciprocal support in 66:4.
rows.anchor: و «الظهير» المعين، ومنه قوله عز وجل وإن تظاهرا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs recognized inimitability immediately through linguistic instinct; later readers reached certainty through inference, as companions directly witnessed prophetic law while later generations learned by transmission.
rows.anchor: فهمت العرب بخلوص فهمها في ميز الكلام ودربتها به ما لا نفهمه نحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like magic in Moses’ time and medicine in Jesus’, rhetoricians directly perceived this miracle; opponents chose violence though they could have answered the challenge, which applies equally to ten or one sura.
rows.anchor: وفهم إعجاز القرآن أرباب الفصاحة الذين لهم غرائب في ميز الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says only an outsider would deny disconnected exceptions in the Qurʾān, noting a view attributed to Ibn Khuwayz Mindad.
rows.anchor: ولا ينكر وقوع المنقطع في القرآن إلا أعجمي، وقد حكي ذلك عن ابن خويز منداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of Arab instinct include using ‘visited the graves’ in 102:2 to infer eventual departure, as well as sharp exchanges among poets and grammarians.
rows.anchor: وألا ترى إلى استدلال الآخر على البعث بقوله حتى زرتم المقابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their spontaneous speech could surpass polished poetry; memorable answers show Arabic eloquence had reached its peak.
rows.anchor: ومن فهمهم أنهم ببدائههم يأتون بكلمة منثورة تفضل المنقح من الشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Challenges to ten suras and one sura test the same matter: composition and arrangement.
rows.anchor: وكذلك التحدي بالعشر السور، والتحدي بالسورة إنما وقع كله على حد واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ten-sura challenge mentions fabrication because Quraysh had called the Qurʾān fabricated; the single-sura challenge omits it in that context.
rows.anchor: في النظم خاصة، وقيد العشر بالافتراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the sura challenge first required matching composition, unseen reports, and other qualities, then shifted to fabricated speech; other accounts collapse on examination.
rows.anchor: فقيل دعوا إلى السورة المماثلة في النظم والغيوب وغير ذلك من الأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse highlights God’s favor in the Qurʾān and rebukes unbelievers; ṣarrafnā means repeatedly explaining an idea in varied ways.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية تنبه على فضل الله في القرآن على العالم، وتوبيخ للكفار منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most readers double rāʾ in ṣarrafnā; al-Hasan reads it light with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «صرفنا» بتشديد الراء، وقرأ الحسن «صرفنا» بفتح الراء خفيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min kull mathal may mark origin with an omitted object, or be an extra particle meaning every parable, as in 2:125.
rows.anchor: وقوله من كل مثل يجوز أن تكون من لابتداء الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They refused means unbelievers chose disbelief and turned from faith; disbelief by creation is God’s act, while acquisition and persistence are human acts.
rows.anchor: وقوله فأبى عبارة عن تكسب الكفار الكفر وإعراضهم عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kufūr is a verbal noun like khurūj.
rows.anchor: وكفورا مصدر كالخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readers differ on tafjur and tufajjir; infa jarat in 2:60 supports the latter form, while the former conveys intensification.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر «حتى تفجر»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanbūʿ is a spring, an emphatic form for abundant water; Quraysh asked for one at Mecca, where earth means their local setting.
rows.anchor: و «الينبوع» الماء النابع، وهي صفة مبالغة إنما تقع للماء الكثير

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi is reported to read ḥabba where most read janna.
rows.anchor: وقرأ «حبة» المهدوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is likewise requested at arid Mecca; tafjīr intensifies rather than makes the verb transitive, and khilālahā means inside or between it.
rows.anchor: وقوله فتفجر. تضعيف مبالغة لا تضعيف تعدية، كغلقت الأبواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Quraysh elders including ʿUtba and Shayba ibn Rabiʿa, ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayya, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith offered kingship, wealth, or treatment before making their demands.
rows.anchor: أن عتبة وشيبة ابني ربيعة، وعبد الله بن أبي أمية، والنضر بن الحارث
